holding_summary: Domicile determination for transfer-tax purposes; decedent's occupancy of an apartment in a New York hotel is mentioned only as evidence of a retained 'home' bearing on domicile, not as a lodging arrangement in dispute.
notes: Domicile/tax case; apartment-hotel tenancy mentioned only in passing to establish a 'permanent home' for domicile analysis, not adjudicating letting practice or its regulation.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
holding_summary: Restrictive building-setback covenant between adjoining lot owners in a residential subdivision; enforced as written against a house built too close to the boundary line.
notes: Pure restrictive-covenant/set-back dispute between neighbors; no compensated occupancy, lodging, or boarding-house issue present.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Term, First Department
holding_summary: Civil Rights Law discrimination action against a saloon; court holds a saloon is a 'place of public accommodation' under ejusdem generis, distinguishing hotels/inns (which furnish lodging) from saloons/restaurants (which do not).
notes: Discusses the definitional line between inns/hotels and saloons only to resolve a race-discrimination claim; does not address householder letting or boarding-house regulation.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Term, First Department
holding_summary: Ordinary apartment lease rent dispute; landlord entitled to a full month's rent in advance despite a later constructive eviction claim for lack of heat, absent a pleaded counterclaim.
notes: Standard landlord-tenant rent/eviction dispute on a conventional apartment lease; no boarding, lodging, or short-term letting practice at issue.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Fourth Department
holding_summary: Restrictive covenant limiting a lot to 'a dwelling and the usual outbuildings'; a physician's addition built and used as a hospital violates the covenant even though incidental medical/surgical use within a dwelling would not.
notes: Dwelling-vs-hospital restrictive covenant case; no compensated lodging, boarding, or letting of rooms is at issue.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Term, Second Department
holding_summary: No implied warranty of habitability attaches to a whole-house farm-dwelling lease absent fraud or express covenant; tenant takes at his peril. Court distinguishes this whole-house lease from cases involving lodgings of rooms in tenements/apartment houses.
notes: Case concerns a conventional whole-dwelling farm lease; the reference to room/apartment lodgings (Streep v. Simpson) is a distinguishing citation only, not an adjudicated fact of this case.

court: Supreme Court, Trial Term, Kings County
holding_summary: Ejectment/charitable-trust case interpreting a donor's conveyance and agreement regarding continued use of a kindergarten-school building; court finds the contingency (general adoption of kindergarten teaching) had occurred, ending defendant's right of occupancy.
notes: Charitable-use/ejectment case about a kindergarten building; no compensated occupancy of a dwelling or lodging practice involved.

court: Supreme Court, Special Term, Oneida County
holding_summary: Housing Act residence-district zoning ordinance (barring commercial buildings, here an undertaking business, from a designated residential block) held unconstitutional as an uncompensated taking not sustainable under the police power.
notes: Zoning/police-power case concerning conversion of a residence into an undertaking business; does not address lodging, boarding, or short-term letting of dwellings.

court: Supreme Court, Special Term, New York County
holding_summary: Sanitary Code ordinance requiring muzzled dogs on public streets upheld as a valid health regulation within the Board of Health's police-power authority.
notes: Dog-muzzling ordinance/habeas corpus case; entirely unrelated to lodging or boarding-house regulation.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Fourth Department
holding_summary: Civil Rights Law discrimination action against a dance hall; court holds dance halls are not a 'place of public accommodation, resort or amusement' under the statute, and in any event no tender of the admission fee was made.
notes: Discusses the statutory definition of 'inn, tavern or hotel...for transient guests' only to bound the reach of the civil-rights statute as applied to a dance hall; no lodging/boarding practice adjudicated.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
holding_summary: Restrictive covenant listing prohibited uses (including 'boarding house') in a residential subdivision; court holds a small private lean-to garage attached to a dwelling is not within the covenant's prohibition under ejusdem generis. No boarding-house use was actually at issue.
notes: 'Boarding house' appears only as one item in a long list of uses prohibited by the recorded covenant; the actual dispute and holding concern a private garage, not any letting or boarding practice, so this is a passing mention rather than an adjudication.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Negotiable Instruments Law case on a forged check cashed by a hotel company acting as payee/holder in due course; drawee bank bears the loss under the Price v. Neal rule.
notes: Commercial-paper/forgery case; the parties' residence in an 'apartment hotel' is incidental background, not an adjudicated lodging or letting arrangement.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Term, First Department
holding_summary: Assignee of a commercial lease held liable for rent based on landlord's consent to the assignment and a prior summary-proceeding final order conclusive on the landlord-tenant relationship.
notes: Ordinary commercial lease-assignment/rent-collection case; no lodging, boarding, or short-term occupancy issue.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Municipal ordinance barring garage permits within 50 feet of a school upheld as a valid fire-safety police-power regulation; permit denial affirmed.
notes: Garage-permit/fire-safety regulation case; unrelated to lodging or boarding-house regulation.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
holding_summary: In a wife's action for judicial separation, the court holds that a husband who supports the family has the right to decide who may reside in the home and may refuse to let his wife keep a boarder or let a furnished room to supplement household income; his exercise of that right did not amount to cruel and inhuman treatment.

quotes.text: To eke out the income, the wife took a boarder, and let out a furnished room.

But the husband who maintains the family has a right to say who shall reside with them in the home, and may refuse to have boarders whose requirements interfere with the family comfort and whose presence excites comment on the part of the neighbors.

notes: Household-economy letting (boarder plus a let furnished room) is treated by the court as an ordinary, unobjectionable domestic practice, but the case does not legally classify the arrangement (lease/license/lodging) since the holding turns on matrimonial law (husband's authority over the household), not property or regulatory doctrine; characterization left null accordingly. Duration of occupancy not specified in the facts as reported.

holding_summary: Domicile determination for transfer-tax purposes; decedent's furnished house in Newport is evidence of a retained domicile, not a lodging or boarding arrangement.
notes: Domicile/tax case; ownership and maintenance of a furnished family residence is discussed only for domicile analysis, not letting practice.

holding_summary: Contested will proceeding; testatrix found to have had testamentary capacity and the will is admitted to probate.
notes: Will-contest/testamentary-capacity case; no connection to lodging, boarding, or dwelling-letting practice.

court: Supreme Court, Special Term for Trials, Kings County
holding_summary: Specific performance of a real-estate purchase contract denied under the unclean-hands doctrine, where plaintiff procured the contract from an elderly, impaired vendor through overreaching and sharp practice.
notes: Plaintiff's occupation running a boarding house is mentioned only as background character/financial-responsibility evidence in a fraud/specific-performance dispute; the boarding-house business itself is not adjudicated, so this is a passing mention.
